cards.title: Knolling Object
cards.description: Deconstructs a single object into its logical component parts. Creates an exploded-view style knolling showing internal structure and assembly.
cards.prompt:
Based on this image:

**KNOLLING OBJECT DECONSTRUCTION**

Analyze the object in the image and generate a knolling board displaying all its component parts in a logical, exploded arrangement.

**Deconstruction Protocol:**
1. **Identify the object type:** Mechanical, electronic, organic, composite
2. **Determine logical disassembly:** What parts can be separated?
3. **Categorize components:**
   - Structural elements (frame, body, housing)
   - Mechanical parts (gears, hinges, fasteners)
   - Electronic components (if applicable)
   - Consumable/replaceable parts
   - Decorative elements

**Disassembly Logic:**
- Follow actual assembly/disassembly sequence
- Group related parts together
- Show fasteners near their corresponding parts
- Maintain left-to-right or top-to-bottom assembly flow
- Smallest components (screws, washers) arranged in neat rows

**Knolling Rules:**
- Neutral grey background (#d0d0d0)
- All parts at strict 90° angles to frame edges
- No overlapping — clear separation between all items
- Parts cleaned and displayed at optimal viewing angle
- Scale preserved — show actual size relationships
- Shadow direction consistent (soft, upper-left source)

**Output Composition:**
- Overhead camera, perpendicular to surface
- Main body/housing positioned centrally or upper-left
- Components radiate outward in logical groups
- Include subtle part-count impression (the satisfaction of seeing everything)
- High detail on textures, wear marks, material qualities

Generate as a technical flat lay photograph with museum-quality precision.

cards.description: Deconstructs an entire scene or environment into categorized object groups. Separates architectural elements, furniture, props, and atmospheric details into a taxonomic flat lay.
cards.prompt:
Based on this image:

**KNOLLING SCENE DECONSTRUCTION**

Analyze the scene/environment in the image and generate a knolling board displaying all identifiable elements organized into 5 distinct categories.

**Scene Analysis Protocol:**
1. **Survey the environment type:** Interior, exterior, urban, rural, industrial, domestic
2. **Identify all discrete elements** that could theoretically be isolated
3. **Assign to exactly 5 categories** (no more, no less)

**Category Framework Examples:**

FOR EXTERIOR/URBAN SCENES:
- Category A: ARCHITECTURE (buildings, structures, facades, doorways)
- Category B: STREET FURNITURE (benches, bins, bollards, signage)
- Category C: VEHICLES (cars, bikes, any transport)
- Category D: INFRASTRUCTURE (poles, wires, road sections, drains)
- Category E: NATURE/ORGANIC (trees, plants, birds, sky elements)

FOR INTERIOR/DOMESTIC SCENES:
- Category A: FURNITURE (major pieces — bed, sofa, table, chairs)
- Category B: WALL ELEMENTS (posters, art, mirrors, clocks, switches)
- Category C: LIGHTING (lamps, fixtures, candles, windows as light sources)
- Category D: TEXTILES (rugs, curtains, cushions, blankets)
- Category E: OBJECTS/DECOR (books, plants, ornaments, personal items)

**Knolling Rules:**
- Neutral background (#c8c8c8)
- Image divided into 5 horizontal rows OR 5 labeled zones
- Each category clearly separated with visual breathing room
- Items within categories arranged at 90° angles
- NO overlapping between any elements
- Scale adjusted for composition (miniaturized buildings, proportional small items)
- Largest/most significant item per category anchors that row

**Output Composition:**
- Overhead view, flat perspective
- Each category row labeled with small, clean typography (optional)
- Consistent lighting across all elements
- Elements should look like architectural model pieces or props
- Total composition fills frame with balanced density

Generate as a taxonomic inventory photograph — every element of the scene laid bare.

All items in pure white and off-white variants. Cream, ivory, bone, chalk, porcelain. Background: light grey to separate objects. Hospital sterile. Objects feel sanitized, specimens, forensic evidence bags. Texture and form dominate. Ghost version of the original.

3. **SINGLE HUE SPECTRUM (Monochromatic Gradient)**
Choose ONE color (specify: red, blue, green, etc.). All items rendered in variations of that single hue — from near-black deep tones to pale tints. Background: complementary neutral. Creates a color study, like a Pantone exploration. Objects unified by hue, differentiated by saturation/value.

---

**ROW 2 — PALETTE MANIPULATIONS:**

4. **INVERTED/NEGATIVE**
Colors flipped to their photographic negative. Blue becomes orange, red becomes cyan, dark becomes light. Background inverts too. Unsettling, alien, like looking at an X-ray of the style. Objects feel like they're from a parallel dimension.

---

**ROW 3 — MATERIAL TRANSFORMATIONS:**

All items rendered in metallic finishes. Specify: GOLD (warm, luxurious, baroque), SILVER (cold, futuristic, clinical), COPPER (warm, industrial, steampunk), or MIXED (each item different metal). Heaviest layering, maximum protection. Swap items for: insulated outerwear, thermal layers, waterproof boots, wool accessories (gloves, scarf, beanie). Colors shift darker, richer. 2. **HOLIDAY WINTER (Festive)**
Winter weight but with celebratory accents. Keep silhouette cozy but add: velvet textures, metallic touches, richer colors (burgundy, forest green, gold). Add objects: gift wrap fragment, invitation card, cocktail napkin. Background: deep green or burgundy. The "office party to family dinner" version. Elevated, intentional, slightly dressy.

3. **LATE WINTER (Thaw Pending)**
Transitional. Lighter layers starting to appear under heavy coat. Mix of winter staples and early spring optimism. Add: umbrella, waterproof layer, transitional boots. Colors: grey, navy, emerging pastels. Background: slate grey. Puddle-ready. The "sick of winter but not risking it" version.

---

**ROW 2 — SPRING/SUMMER ARC:**

4. **EARLY SPRING (Cautious Emergence)**
Layers that can be added/removed. Light jacket over lighter layers. Swap heavy boots for transitional footwear. Colors brighten: soft blues, greens, creams. Add: sunglasses, allergy medication implied, light scarf. Background: soft sage. The "might be warm, might snow" version. Hopeful but prepared.

5. **PEAK SUMMER (Heat Maximum)**
Minimum viable coverage. Lightest fabrics, most skin, breathable everything. Swap for: shorts/skirt, sandals or light sneakers, tank or linen shirt. Add: sunscreen, water bottle, sweat-wicking items. Colors: whites, naturals, bright accents. Background: warm cream. The "function over form, survival over style" version.

6. **LATE SUMMER (Golden Hour)**
Still warm but richer. Summer items in harvest tones — amber, terracotta, olive, cream. Slightly more coverage returning. Add: light cardigan for evening, warmer accessories. Background: wheat/golden. The "last beach weekend" version. Nostalgic summer, golden light, end-of-season energy.

---

**ROW 3 — AUTUMN DESCENT:**

7. **EARLY AUTUMN (Crisp Optimism)**
The favorite season version. Perfect layering weather. Swap for: medium-weight jacket, boots return, scarves for style not survival. Colors: rust, burgundy, camel, olive. Add: coffee cup ring stain, fallen leaf. Background: warm taupe. The "finally can wear real clothes" version. Cozy but not heavy.

8. **DEEP AUTUMN (Pre-Winter)**
Darker, heavier, preparing for cold. Substantial coat, heavier boots, gloves appearing. Colors deepen: charcoal, brown, deep red. Add: tissues, umbrella, comfort items. Background: dark brown. Rain-ready, wind-resistant. The "denial about winter" version.

9. **EXTREME WEATHER (Climate Event)**
Pick a weather extreme and adapt: HEATWAVE (emergency cooling, minimal layers, wet towel), MONSOON (full waterproofing, sealed bags, rain boots), DUST STORM (face coverage, goggles, sealed layers), HUMID TROPICAL (anti-moisture, breathable mesh, moisture-wicking everything). Background matches climate. The "survival" version.

---

**Technical Execution:**
- All 9 boards maintain same arrangement logic
- Object SUBSTITUTION not just color change — different actual items per season
- Style DNA must remain recognizable (same subculture/aesthetic, different expression)
- Consistent overhead lighting, temperature-appropriate color grading
- Final output: 3x3 contact sheet showing full seasonal wardrobe

**TO USE:**
1. Provide source image OR describe the base style/knolling
2. Specify if any items are "sacred" (must appear in all seasons)
3. For #9 (Extreme): specify the weather event
4. Indicate geographic context (affects seasonal interpretation)

- Do not redesign the tattoo.

- Keep the original tattoo identity, imperfections and proportions.

**EQUIRECTANGULAR PROJECTION — TECHNICAL SPEC:**

**VISUAL CHARACTERISTICS OF EQUIRECTANGULAR:**
- Aspect ratio: EXACTLY 2:1 (example: 4096×2048, 8192×4096)

- Upright vertical scene edges map to vertical meridians when the panorama is level

- Left and right edges = the SAME point in space (seamless wrap)

- Objects at horizon level (middle band) appear most natural

- NOT a fisheye (fisheye is circular, equirectangular is rectangular 2:1)
- NOT a wide panorama crop (those don't cover full 180° vertical)
- NOT a perspective photo with wide lens
- NOT curved at the sides like barrel distortion

**REFERENCE:** Google "equirectangular projection" or "HDRI environment map" — the output should look exactly like those examples.

**SEAMLESS WRAP:**
- Left edge and right edge must be IDENTICAL (they represent same point in 360° space)
- When wrapped into a sphere, no visible seam
- Test: mentally scroll image left-to-right in loop — transition must be invisible

**FIDELITY:**
- Extend source environment faithfully — don't invent major elements
- Match materials, colors, lighting throughout 360°
- Keep unseen areas simple if not evidenced in source

**COLOR GRADING LOCK:**
- EXACT color grade from source across entire panorama

**EQUIRECTANGULAR PROJECTION — TECHNICAL SPEC:**

This is a SPECIFIC projection format used for HDRI, VR, and 3D environment maps.

**VISUAL CHARACTERISTICS OF EQUIRECTANGULAR:**
- Aspect ratio: EXACTLY 2:1 (example: 4096×2048, 8192×4096)
- The level horizon stays straight; other straight horizontal scene edges generally curve under spherical projection
- Upright vertical scene edges map to vertical meridians when the panorama is level
- Top edge = ceiling directly above camera (zenith) — appears STRETCHED horizontally
- Bottom edge = floor directly below camera (nadir) — appears STRETCHED horizontally
- Left and right edges = the SAME point in space (seamless wrap)
- Objects near top/bottom edges appear horizontally stretched/distorted
- Objects at horizon level (middle band) appear most natural

**WHAT EQUIRECTANGULAR IS NOT:**
- NOT a fisheye (fisheye is circular, equirectangular is rectangular 2:1)
- NOT a wide panorama crop (those don't cover full 180° vertical)
- NOT a perspective photo with wide lens
- NOT curved at the sides like barrel distortion

**REFERENCE:** Google "equirectangular projection" or "HDRI environment map" — the output should look exactly like those examples.

**SEAMLESS WRAP:**
- Left edge and right edge must be IDENTICAL (they represent same point in 360° space)
- When wrapped into a sphere, no visible seam

- Aspect ratio: EXACTLY 2:1 (example: 4096×2048, 8192×4096)

- NOT a fisheye (fisheye is circular, equirectangular is rectangular 2:1)
- NOT a wide panorama crop (those don't cover full 180° vertical)
- NOT a perspective photo with wide lens
